translationRepairs: His father Yun Sheng had taken his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of the Qianlong reign and advanced from Hanlin compiler to Vice Minister of War.
His father Yunsheng had taken his jinshi degree in the sixtieth year of the Qianlong reign and advanced from Hanlin compiler to Vice Minister of War.

s0002 names the father 允升 as one given name; spacing it Yun Sheng invents a two-part Western personal name. Unspaced Yunsheng matches the Chinese and the parallel given-name claim already recorded as Yunsheng.

Fengbiao joined Ministers Weng Qing, Quan Qing, and Wang Qingyun in a joint memorial: "Huai'an is ground the rebels are certain to contest; if their forces cross the river, the people of Henan and Shandong will be thrown into alarm and suppression will become far more difficult.

Fengbiao joined Minister Wenqing and Vice Ministers Quanqing and Wang Qingyun in a joint memorial: "Huai'an is ground the rebels are certain to contest; if their forces cross the river, the people of Henan and Shandong will be thrown into alarm and suppression will become far more difficult.
s0111 has 尚書文慶，侍郎全慶、王慶雲: 文慶 romanizes as Wenqing (not Weng Qing), 全慶 as Quanqing, and only Wenqing is 尚書 while Quanqing and Wang Qingyun are 侍郎. The proposed titles and names restore that reading.
In the seventh year of Tongzhi, As Minister of Personnel he was made Associate Grand Secretary and also chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
In the seventh year of Tongzhi, as Minister of Personnel he was made Associate Grand Secretary and also chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
s0127 is continuous prose (同治七年，以吏部尚書…); capital As after the comma is only an English capitalization error, and lowercase as is the correct fix without changing meaning.

He also reported that resistance to tax collection and arrest had become widespread near the capital because unfit men held local office, and ordered governors-general and governors to select officials impartially without favoritism.

He also reported that resistance to tax collection and arrest had become widespread near the capital because unfit men held local office, and asked that governors-general and governors be instructed to select officials impartially without favoritism.

In s0089 又言…諭各督撫 is still memorial language asking the throne to instruct the governors-general and governors; 諭 is the imperial directive requested, not an order Zhou himself issued. The proposed wording correctly restores that agency.
